entities.name: Pedro Fernandez de Frias
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pedro Fernandez de Frias, a prominent Castilian cardinal, played a significant, albeit shifting, role in the tumultuous ecclesiastical landscape of the late 14th and early 15th centuries, culminating in his death on September 28, 1420. His career was inextricably linked to the Western Schism (1378-1417), a period of profound division within the Catholic Church that saw rival popes claim legitimacy from Rome and Avignon. Initially a staunch supporter of the Avignon papacy, specifically Antipope Benedict XIII (Pedro de Luna), Fernandez de Frias navigated the complex political and spiritual allegiances of the time, eventually contributing to the schism's resolution.

Born into a noble Castilian family, Fernandez de Frias rose through the ecclesiastical ranks, serving as Bishop of Osma from 1379 and later as Archbishop of Seville from 1394. His elevation to cardinal by Benedict XIII in 1405 underscored his importance within the Avignon curia and his influence in the Iberian Peninsula. For years, he was a key figure in the efforts to maintain Benedict XIII's authority, even as European powers increasingly withdrew their obedience from the Avignon line. His diplomatic and administrative acumen were crucial in sustaining the Avignon cause, particularly within the Crown of Castile, which remained a significant stronghold.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pedro Fernandez de Frias's pivotal shift from supporting Benedict XIII to recognizing the Council of Constance was instrumental in consolidating the unified papacy and reintegrating Spanish ecclesiastical structures, thereby contributing significantly to the resolution of the Western Schism.
